name: Orliny Pereval
historical_basis: Caucasus foothills, August-October 1942: the fight for the high passes during Operation Edelweiss (Klukhor, Marukh, Sancharo) - a fictional pass composed for mirror fairness; no specific engagement is depicted.
design_notes: an east-west mountain wall sits ON the mirror axis and is impassable except at three gates - the wide Dolina meadow col (west), the high pass carrying the hamlet of Orlinoye (center), and the rocky defile (east); the three gates ARE the three lanes

the two summits (Sokol west, Oryol east) stand on the axis, contested equally, but are reachable ONLY through the pass col - taking the middle unlocks the high ground, and the high ground dominates both flanks
1000m x 1000m at 5m height samples, mirror-symmetric across the axis; DRY map by design - a single global water level cannot perch a mountain tarn, and the highland reads honest without one

features.name: Orliny massif
features.note: the mountain wall between the teams: impassable by design except at the three gates - its grade is the map's real border

features.name: Sokol summit
features.note: the western summit: reachable only along the crest walk from the pass col; overlooks the Dolina lane

features.name: Oryol summit
features.note: the eastern summit, the roof of the map: reachable only along the crest walk; overlooks the pass approaches and the defile

features.name: Dolina meadow col
features.note: the wide western gate: fast, open, and watched from the shoulder shelves and the rim

features.name: the defile
features.note: the narrow eastern gate: a rocky slot with short sightlines - the knife-fight lane

features.name: Dolina meadows
features.note: the low western corridor: meadow floor with oak groves and hedgerow screens for the run to the col

features.name: hamlet of Orlinoye
features.note: a mirrored hamlet on the pass bench; the chapel on the axis is the tallest silhouette of the col
